node-1.label: A 49-year-old woman presented with healed ulcers of the lower lip and nasal dorsum and a nonhealing ulcer of the left lateral infraorbital area

node-2.label: Patient reported several years of facial ulcers described as 'scratches' developing over weeks to months into red, indurated, tender ulcers that finally crusted and healed

node-3.label: Review of systems was positive for dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, mild hand and ankle swelling, and dysphagia

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed healed ulcers on lower lip and nasal dorsum and a nonhealing ulcer in left lateral infraorbital area

node-5.label: Later ocular findings included diplopia, sense of fullness below left eye, restriction of left eye into hypotropic and exotropic position, full-thickness defect through lateral lower eyelid, exposed conjunctiva and bony orbital rim

attrs.why: Expert analyses from the laboratory physician and pathologist reaffirm that positive ANA 1:360, low C4, sicca/Raynaud/arthralgia, granulomatous inflammation, and negative cultures favor an autoimmune/granulomatous process as the most credible hypothesis. They also note that negative ANCA tempers vasculitis, and that missing anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, RF, Schirmer test, salivary flow, and chest CT hilar lymph node assessment limit further specification. Sarcoidosis and foreign-body reaction remain credible alternatives, so confidence remains 0.60.

Orbital biopsy demonstrates granulomatous inflammation with foreign-body giant cells rather than a malignant cellular proliferation, and microbiologic cultures are negative. Combined with the chronic healing/crusting ulcer pattern, this new pathologic and laboratory evidence argues strongly against cutaneous/orbital malignancy, so confidence is reduced from 0.25 to 0.08.

Microbiologic cultures are negative and biopsy shows granulomatous (non-infectious) inflammation; no organism has been identified. Together with the chronic healing ulcer pattern and systemic autoimmune features, this new information strongly refutes a chronic infectious etiology, so confidence is reduced from 0.20 to 0.07.

node-10.label: Serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level is elevated

node-13.label: Orbital biopsy reveals foreign-body granulomas containing polarizable material

attrs.why: Expert analyses explicitly sustain sarcoidosis: elevated ACE, granulomatous orbital biopsy, and negative ANCA are supportive. However, chest CT for hilar lymphadenopathy and serum calcium data are missing, preventing confirmation. Positive ANA and low C4 keep autoimmune/vasculitic disease more likely, so confidence remains 0.35.

attrs.why: Orbital biopsy shows foreign-body granulomas containing polarizable material, the hallmark of a foreign-body reaction, and expert analyses maintain this as a credible alternative. Yet no trauma, foreign-body, or filler exposure history is documented, and no foreign material source is identified, so confidence remains 0.30.

node-18.label: Chest CT for hilar lymphadenopathy has not been performed

node-19.label: No documented history of trauma or foreign-body/filler exposure

node-20.label: Direct immunofluorescence, salivary biopsy, and serum calcium testing data are missing

attrs.why: Dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, and positive ANA with low C4 are compatible with an autoimmune sicca syndrome. Expert analyses from the laboratory physician and pathologist specifically highlight that anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, RF, Schirmer test, and salivary flow measurement are missing, preventing confirmation of Sjögren syndrome. Facial ulcers and orbital granulomatous inflammation are atypical, so confidence remains 0.28.

Positive ANA (1:360), low C4, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, and facial ulcers could fit systemic lupus erythematosus, and expert analyses note that anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm are missing. Granulomatous orbital inflammation and foreign-body material are atypical, so confidence is 0.25.

The frontier autoimmune/vasculitic disease is too general and can be refined into a specific autoimmune connective-tissue entity. Dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, dysphagia, ANA 1:360, and low C4 are compatible with Sjögren syndrome as a fine-grained subcategory. Expert analyses emphasize that anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, RF, Schirmer test, and salivary flow measurement are still missing, preventing confirmation, so confidence remains moderate at 0.28.

As a further refinement of 'autoimmune/vasculitic disease' (node-6), SLE is supported by node-9 (positive ANA 1:360 with decreased C4), node-3 (Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, oral/dryness symptoms) and node-2 (chronic facial ulcers). Missing anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm (node-17) and atypical orbital granulomatous inflammation (node-12) limit this subcategory, giving confidence 0.25.

The frontier explicitly includes 'vasculitic', so a specific small-vessel vasculitis is the logical next-level hypothesis. Node-4 and node-5 (destructive facial/nasal ulcers with full-thickness orbital and eyelid defects) are classic for granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and node-12 (granulomatous inflammation) fits. However, node-11 (negative ANCA) and the lymphoplasmacytic sicca picture reduce its likelihood.

Refining 'autoimmune/vasculitic disease' (node-6), IgG4-related disease can cause chronic orbital inflammation with granulomatous and foreign-body giant-cell features on biopsy (node-12, node-13) and elevated inflammatory markers. No serum IgG4 or specific histopathologic IgG4 data are available (nodes 17,20), so confidence remains low.

node-3.label: Review of systems was positive for dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, mild hand and ankle swelling, and dysphagia

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed healed ulcers on lower lip and nasal dorsum and a nonhealing ulcer in left lateral infraorbital area

node-5.label: Later ocular findings included diplopia, sense of fullness below left eye, restriction of left eye into hypotropic and exotropic position, full-thickness defect through lateral lower eyelid, exposed conjunctiva and bony orbital rim

attrs.why: Expert analyses from the laboratory physician and pathologist reaffirm that positive ANA 1:360, low C4, sicca/Raynaud/arthralgia, granulomatous inflammation, and negative cultures favor an autoimmune/granulomatous process as the most credible hypothesis. They also note that negative ANCA tempers vasculitis, and that missing anti-dsDNA, anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, RF, Schirmer test, salivary flow, and chest CT hilar lymph node assessment limit further specification. Sarcoidosis and foreign-body reaction remain credible alternatives, so confidence remains 0.60.

Orbital biopsy demonstrates granulomatous inflammation with foreign-body giant cells rather than a malignant cellular proliferation, and microbiologic cultures are negative. Combined with the chronic healing/crusting ulcer pattern, this new pathologic and laboratory evidence argues strongly against cutaneous/orbital malignancy, so confidence is reduced from 0.25 to 0.08.

Microbiologic cultures are negative and biopsy shows granulomatous (non-infectious) inflammation; no organism has been identified. Together with the chronic healing ulcer pattern and systemic autoimmune features, this new information strongly refutes a chronic infectious etiology, so confidence is reduced from 0.20 to 0.07.

node-10.label: Serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) level is elevated

node-13.label: Orbital biopsy reveals foreign-body granulomas containing polarizable material

attrs.why: Expert analyses explicitly sustain sarcoidosis: elevated ACE, granulomatous orbital biopsy, and negative ANCA are supportive. However, chest CT for hilar lymphadenopathy and serum calcium data are missing, preventing confirmation. Positive ANA and low C4 keep autoimmune/vasculitic disease more likely, so confidence remains 0.35.

attrs.why: Orbital biopsy shows foreign-body granulomas containing polarizable material, the hallmark of a foreign-body reaction, and expert analyses maintain this as a credible alternative. Yet no trauma, foreign-body, or filler exposure history is documented, and no foreign material source is identified, so confidence remains 0.30.

node-18.label: Chest CT for hilar lymphadenopathy has not been performed

node-19.label: No documented history of trauma or foreign-body/filler exposure

node-20.label: Direct immunofluorescence, salivary biopsy, and serum calcium testing data are missing

attrs.why: Dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, and positive ANA with low C4 are compatible with an autoimmune sicca syndrome. Expert analyses from the laboratory physician and pathologist specifically highlight that anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, RF, Schirmer test, and salivary flow measurement are missing, preventing confirmation of Sjögren syndrome. Facial ulcers and orbital granulomatous inflammation are atypical, so confidence remains 0.28.

Positive ANA (1:360), low C4, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, and facial ulcers could fit systemic lupus erythematosus, and expert analyses note that anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm are missing. Granulomatous orbital inflammation and foreign-body material are atypical, so confidence is 0.25.

The frontier autoimmune/vasculitic disease is too general and can be refined into a specific autoimmune connective-tissue entity. Dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, dysphagia, ANA 1:360, and low C4 are compatible with Sjögren syndrome as a fine-grained subcategory. Expert analyses emphasize that anti-Ro/SSA, anti-La/SSB, RF, Schirmer test, and salivary flow measurement are still missing, preventing confirmation, so confidence remains moderate at 0.28.

As a further refinement of 'autoimmune/vasculitic disease' (node-6), SLE is supported by node-9 (positive ANA 1:360 with decreased C4), node-3 (Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, oral/dryness symptoms) and node-2 (chronic facial ulcers). Missing anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm (node-17) and atypical orbital granulomatous inflammation (node-12) limit this subcategory, giving confidence 0.25.

The frontier explicitly includes 'vasculitic', so a specific small-vessel vasculitis is the logical next-level hypothesis. Node-4 and node-5 (destructive facial/nasal ulcers with full-thickness orbital and eyelid defects) are classic for granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and node-12 (granulomatous inflammation) fits. However, node-11 (negative ANCA) and the lymphoplasmacytic sicca picture reduce its likelihood.

Refining 'autoimmune/vasculitic disease' (node-6), IgG4-related disease can cause chronic orbital inflammation with granulomatous and foreign-body giant-cell features on biopsy (node-12, node-13) and elevated inflammatory markers. No serum IgG4 or specific histopathologic IgG4 data are available (nodes 17,20), so confidence remains low.
